culturalBackground: In Indonesia, henna is commonly called pacar or inai.
Malam Bainai is a pre-wedding henna night in the Minangkabau tradition of West Sumatra.
The traditional practice is to stain the bride's fingertips and nails red, not to draw fine patterns.
Modern Indonesian bridal henna often borrows Arabic and Indian layouts and is sometimes done in white body paint, which is not true henna.
applicationTips: For the traditional look, cover the fingertips and nails with a thick, even layer of paste.
Keep modern lace-style designs fine and light, with thin lines and small motifs.
White henna is a body paint that sits on the skin; it does not stain and washes off within days.

faqPool.a: It is the henna night held before a Minangkabau wedding in West Sumatra, when henna is applied to the bride's nails and fingertips.
No. It is a cosmetic body paint or adhesive. Real henna always stains in shades of orange to reddish brown.

faqPool.q: What does Indonesian bridal henna look like today?
faqPool.a: Many brides choose fine, lace-like designs on the back of the hand and fingers, often inspired by Arabic and Indian styles.
